reason: The pressed state becomes reachable and visible on all five stateful components (same 0.0.0 baseline as 003 through 009; this declaration advances the sealed candidate, so the cumulative delta stays MAJOR). Five published token names are ADDED - ki.surface.pressed-overlay-inverse, and the primary/secondary active.overlay pair on each of ki-button and ki-icon-button - and none is removed. One published value changes. The rest of the surface delta is the set of CSS custom properties the CEM records each component as CONSUMING. (1) THE DEFECT, and it is not the one the industry research predicted. Every pressed rule in the library was written as :host(:active). :active lands on the element being activated and propagates to the host only for POINTER activation. Measured in Chromium across all five components - host :active false, inner control :active true - so :host(:active) was unreachable CSS for every keyboard user, and no token value could have fixed it. :host(:has(button:active)) cannot bridge it: :has() does not cross the shadow boundary, verified in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. All five components now target their inner control, which receives :active on both the pointer and the keyboard path, with the rules placed after the structural rules they share a target with so specificity still descends down the file. (2) ki-button and ki-icon-button additionally had nothing to show even once reachable: their 15 pressed blocks each set bg/fg/border to -active- tokens that are documented mirrors of rest and then WITHDREW the hover overlay, so the appearance was legible only as the removal of a hover a keyboard or touch user never had. Pressed is now the interaction overlay one rung deeper. TWO rules per component, not one, because each already carries two overlay conventions: primary paints on a dark brand fill and its wash lightens (White/5 hover to White/8 pressed, via the existing ki.state-layer.pressed, which carried a written MarsUI derivation and was consumed by nothing); every other variant paints on a light fill and darkens (Black/3 hover to Black/5 pressed, via the newly minted ki.surface.pressed-overlay-inverse). A single pressed overlay would have LIGHTENED the primary button on press and read as less pressed rather than more - caught by measuring the rendered result, not by reading the tokens. The new semantic role introduces no new value: Black/5 and White/5 are existing primitives, and the rule it states is the one its hover sibling already states. (3) ki-checkbox, ki-switch and ki-radio needed only the selector correction; their pressed values were already designed and merely unreachable without a mouse. One exception: ki.radio.selected.active.bg was {ki.surface.s0}, identical to its own rest fill, so pressing an already-selected option reverted the hover step instead of deepening it - the same pressed-as-un-hover shape, surviving in one cell. It now follows the ramp its unselected sibling already follows (rest s0, hover s1, pressed s2). (4) The forty-five ki.button.<variant>.<tone>.active.{bg,fg,border} tokens, their ki-icon-button twins and the per-variant active.shadow tokens remain PUBLISHED and are now unconsumed. Removing them is a separate change requiring deprecation metadata, deliberately not folded in here. (5) Baselines: no committed screenshot captures a pressed state, so none moves.
